Hi Elena,

Nice catching up on the QBR last week. As you mentioned, Peakseed has been seeing a consistent burst pattern (short, high-concurrency spikes) that drove utilization above the committed baseline in February. I pulled a short usage extract and attached a CSV with per-hour GPU utilization for Feb 1 - Mar 1 to help ground the conversation.

Proposed next steps from my side:
- Quick confirmation call (30m) this week to agree on the immediate top-up pilot (we're thinking +40 GPUs for 6 weeks).
- If pilot metrics look good (p95 latency, queue length, and cost per token within thresholds), convert to a scalable reserve: commit to a smaller baseline + automatic burst pool that scales by policy.

Questions for you today: can you share the target SLA/throughput you want guaranteed during spikes, and whether procurement wants a single amendment vs. a short-term PO for the pilot?

Attaching: peakseed_usage_2028_q1.csv (summary), and I'll drop a draft MUP after chat.

Thanks,

- Procurement prefers a single short amendment if possible. Billing wants clarity on delta for the pilot and if credits apply.

Hi Elena — thanks for the clarity. A couple of technical/ops notes before Tue: 

1) Guardrails: we can apply two short-term mitigations for the pilot: 
   - Batch-job throttling window: limit background batch jobs to a separate pool during 80th-95th percentile hours (configurable).
   - Request-level preemption: mark real-time inference as "high-priority" to push background work to the burst pool.

2) Sizing proposal for pilot: +40 A100-equivalent GPUs, pre-warmed with prefix caching for the top 10 models you run. If peak concurrency stays under 2k and p95 < 800ms, we recommend converting to a 12-month scalable reserve with a baseline of +24 GPUs and a managed burst pool of up to +64 GPUs (policy-triggered).

3) Cost note: pilot incremental cost estimated at $X/day (invoice line item) — I'll route detailed numbers to billing and include a redline-friendly amendment for procurement.

I've attached a draft SOW addendum and a short Mutual Action Plan (MUP) that lays out success metrics and decision gates.

Elena — looping in Grace on the commercial side. I uploaded the amendment template to the Drive link below and drafted a single-amendment flow so procurement can sign once the pilot is approved. Key bullets: 

- Pilot: +40 GPUs for 6 weeks, billed as a one-time top-up line item; refund/credit if we fail the measured SLA gates.
- Conversion trigger: if p95 latency < 800ms and cost per successful request stays within agreed threshold for 2 consecutive weeks, we execute the amendment to a 12-month scalable reserve (baseline +24; burst pool up to +64).
- Cancellation: 7-day notice for early termination of pilot; no penalties besides consumed usage.

Grace — can you confirm the discount band for a 12-month commitment? Elena — if procurement is OK with the single amendment flow, I'll get procurement-ready wording over today.

Marissa Cole
